sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING ON I.A., THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 19.01.2017 passed by Addition Senior Civil Judge and Commissioner for Employees Compensation at Bidar (for short 'Commissioner') in ECA.no.54/2014, this appeal is filed.
2. Shri Santosh Biradar, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants challenging dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2-insurer.

It was submitted that Mohd. Chaoos (workman) was employed as driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing registration no.KA-38/1002, belonging to respondent no.1 (employer) insured with respondent NC:
2023:KHC-K:6494 no.2 (insurer).

It was submitted that as per instructions of employer when workman was driving said Auto Rickshaw on 10.10.2011 loaded with iron rods from Bidar to Bhalki,
vehicle met with accident in which driver sustained fatal injuries.
3. Claiming compensation on account of loss of dependency, his mother and unmarried sister filed petition under Section 10 of Employees Compensation Act, 1897 (for short 'E.C. Act').
4. In said petition, employer and insurer entered appearance and contested it.
Commissioner after framing appropriate issues and recorded evidence, wherein claimant no.1 was examined as PW-1 and Exhibits P1 to P7 were marked.
Respondents did not lead evidence.
5. Commissioner after considering same held that relationship of employer and employee as established and accident occurred in course of and arose out of employment.
It also held that vehicle was covered with policy issued by respondent no.2-insurer as on date of NC: 2023:KHC-K:6494 accident.

However, on ground those claimants failed to establish that deceased driver possessed driving licence as on date of accident, liability of insurer was discharged and employer was held liable to pay compensation.
Commissioner assessed total compensation of Rs.10,85,000/- with interest payable from one month after date of accident.

sentences.text: It was submitted that during evidence, claimants had stated that deceased was possessing driving licence but, same was lost at time of accident.
In view of same and in absence of any specific evidence led by respondents, Commissioner was not justified in discharging liability of insurer.

Relying upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Gurmail Singh @ Gurmer @ Gurnal Singh v/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. and Anr., in Civil Appeal No(s).12065/2018,
disposed of on 13.12.2018 and decision of learned Single Judge of this Court in MFA.no.6488/2010,
disposed of on 23.07.2019, relying NC: 2023:KHC-K:6494 upon Gurmail Singh's case (supra), it was submitted that under similar circumstances award was modified and insurer was held liable to pay compensation to claimant and thereafter recover same from insured.

entities.text: Gurmail Singh @ Gurmer @ Gurnal Singh v/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. In view of above, learned counsel submitted that following substantial question of law would arise for consideration :
"Whether Commissioner was justified in dismissing claim petition against insurer?"
8.
On other hand, Shri Sanjay M. Joshi, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer sought to support award and oppose appeal.

It was submitted that as observed by Commissioner, even in case,
driving licence of deceased was lost at time accident, since claimants were mother and sister of deceased driver, there was no impediment for them to have secure certified copy or extract from RTO and produce same.

In absence, presumption has to be drawn against them and therefore,
award would be justified.

While learned counsel for insurer was not able to dispute legal position in view of Gurmail Singh's case (supra), it was however submitted that award of Commissioner was excessive and would call for reduction.
It was submitted that accident occurred on 10.10.2011.
As on said date, amendment to E.C. Act, inserting Section 4(1B) was in force.

As per Notification no. S.O. 1258(E) dated 31.05.2010,
issued by Central Government, monthly wages of workman for purposes of Sub-section (1) of Section 4 of E.C. Act, was stipulated at Rs.8,000/-.
In view of same, Commissioner was not justified in considering higher monthly income and sought reduction.

10. In reply, learned counsel for claimants submitted that Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jaya Biswal and Ors. v/s Branch Manager, Iffco Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd. and Anr., reported in 2016 (11) SCC 201, had upheld determination of income of Rs.10,000/- in case of driver and therefore, Commissioner did not commit any error.

entities.text: Jaya Biswal and Ors. v/s Branch Manager, Iffco Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd. and Anr., reported in 2016 (11) SCC 201
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was alternatively submitted NC:
2023:KHC-K:6494 that Commissioner had not awarded compensation towards funeral expenses.

11. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
12.

From above submission, since workman is in appeal challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer, substantial questions of law as proposed would arise for consideration:

entities.text: Saleema Bee And Anr vs Babumiya And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Whether Commissioner was justified in not awarding compensation under head of funeral expenses?
13. In view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Gurmail Singh (supra) relied upon by this Court in MFA.no.6488/2010, dismissal of claim petition against insurer would not be justified.
Therefore dismissal of claim petition against insurer would not be justified and respondent no.2-insurer would be liable to pay compensation.
However, Commissioner has assessed monthly income of deceased at Rs.10,000/-.
Though NC: 2023:KHC-K:6494 Hon'ble Supreme Court had affirmed consideration of Rs.10,000/- per month as income of driver, no ratio was laid down in Jaya Biswal's case (supra) in that regard.
In view of notification issued under Section 4(1B) of Employees Compensation Act, assessment of Rs.10,000/- as monthly income by Commissioner would not be justified.
It has to be considered at Rs.8,000/-.
At same time, it is seen that, Commissioner did not award funeral expenses.
In absence of specific evidence, Rs.15,000/- as is awarded in motor vehicle accident cases would be just and proper.

Further, in view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shobha and Ors. v/s The Chairman, Vithalrao Shinde Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Limited and Ors.,
reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 308, interest would be payable from date of accident.

entities.text: Shobha and Ors. v/s The Chairman, Vithalrao Shinde Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Limited and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
Commissioner's award would call for modification as:
Rs.8,000/- x 50% x 216.91 = Rs.8,67,640/-;
And Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6494
Thus, total compensation would be Rs.8,82,640/-.
Substantial question of law is answered as above.

14. Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. Claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,82,640/- with interest at 12%
p.a. from date of accident i.e., 10.10.2011 till deposit.
iii. Dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2 is set aside.

Respondent no.2-insurer is held liable to pay compensation and shall deposit said compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. Liberty is reserved to insurer to recover compensation amount from insured after satisfying award.

Sd/-
